text:
Philly Hockey Now called Denver Barkey the Flyers' "'Poster Child' of Doing the Small Things," and his numbers back the description. The 21-year-old, a third-round pick in 2023, plays about 14 and a half minutes a night, and Philadelphia takes 53.7% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, 12 points better than without him.

The scoring has come along too: 4 goals and 11 points in 21 games, all four goals in his last ten. Some of that is running hot. He's shooting 20% on just 20 shots, and his top shot speed ranks near the bottom of the league. His job is creating for others and keeping chances away, not finishing.

That defensive side was there last season too: Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting fewer chances with him on (91st percentile among forwards), the bulk of his 0.8 wins above replacement. He picked up an assist in his return Tuesday after missing a game. Watch whether the Flyers keep trusting him on the power play, where 5 of his points have come.
